title: The AI usage bonus
scenario:
You are head of sales operations at a medical-supplies distributor with 120 reps in 12 regions. The COO wants to speed up AI adoption and has a plan with a leaderboard and a bonus.

Finance also worries about cost. The exhibit shows the plan, a sample of the dashboard and two comments.
exhibit:
COO plan (made-up example data)
  - Leaderboard of reps by messages sent to the AI assistant
  - Bonus for the top 10 reps by messages
  - Minimum of 50 messages a week for every rep
  - Weekly CSV export of all 120 reps sent to the 12 regional managers

Sample week
  Rep    Messages    Meetings booked    AI errors reported
  Ana    410         3                  0
  Ben    95          9                  4
  Cai    40          8                  1
  Dev    280         4                  0

Comments
  Regional manager: "Ben's error reports make our region look bad. Tell him
  to stop sending them."
  Finance: "We used 92% of the contract's credits this month. We need a
  hard stop before the limit, not a nudge."

questions.prompt: What should the bonus be based on?

options.text: Messages sent, because it is the easiest number to count and to compare between all of the reps.
options.explanation: Ana sends the most messages and books 3 meetings; Ben sends 95 and books 9. OpenAI's page says a message count doesn't show how much work was finished.

options.text: Days logged in to the assistant each month, because it rewards steady use more than raw volume.
options.explanation: Logging in is still activity. A person can log in each day and book no more meetings.

options.text: Meetings booked, rewarded at team level against last quarter, with customer errors as a guard.
options.explanation: Right. This pays for a team outcome against a baseline, and a guard number shows if the outcome costs quality. This is our course guidance, in line with the vendors' advice to pair usage with outcomes.

options.text: Each rep's rank on the dashboard leaderboard at the end of every month, as shown to all reps.
options.explanation: Anthropic's page uses the leaderboard to find people who can share techniques. A rank on usage is still a rank on activity.

questions.prompt: A regional manager wants Ben to stop reporting AI errors. What is the best response?

options.text: Tell the manager Ben's reports protect customers, and track how fast causes get fixed.
options.explanation: Right. Chapter 2 put human review where it matters; reviewers will find errors. Counting reports as a good sign is course guidance, not a vendor rule.

options.text: Ask Ben to report errors only to his manager, so that the other regions in the company never see them.
options.explanation: Hiding reports keeps the errors in place and removes the evidence the whole company needs.

options.text: Rank regions by the number of reports and give the region with the most reports a warning.
options.explanation: That punishes the regions that report, so reports would stop and errors would go to customers.

options.text: Remove error reporting from the plan, because reports are not a business outcome.
options.explanation: A wrong output sent to a customer is a business cost. A guard number needs the reports.

questions.prompt: Finance wants a hard stop before credits run out. Which control fits?

options.text: A usage alert at 80%, which will make managers slow down their teams a little.
options.explanation: OpenAI's guide says alerts notify but don't stop spending.

options.text: A bonus for reps whose usage stays low, so that they save credits themselves.
options.explanation: A bonus is an incentive, not a control. The guide says guidance doesn't replace an enforced limit.

options.text: A smaller default model for everyone, because defaults make people use less.
options.explanation: OpenAI's guide says a model default can influence consumption but does not replace an enforced limit.

options.text: Enforced user usage limits and a workspace overage limit, set before the cap.
options.explanation: Right. The ChatGPT docs separate enforced limits from alerts and guidance. Anthropic's admin guide also lists spend limits and rate limits.

questions.prompt: Who should receive the weekly CSV with names of all 120 reps?

options.text: All 12 regional managers, so that they can rank their own reps in public.
options.explanation: The ChatGPT docs say reports are identifiable organizational data. Wide, public ranking is the opposite of care.

options.text: A few named support staff see names; managers get team totals only.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI's page says to treat downloaded reports as identifiable data under access and retention policy. A small group for support and team aggregates for managers is our suggested default.

options.text: Nobody; the firm should stop collecting usage data, so that no one can see it.
options.explanation: Both vendors offer admin analytics to see adoption. The point is to limit who sees names, not to stop collecting data.

options.text: Every employee, so that reps can compare themselves with their colleagues.
options.explanation: Sharing everyone's usage with everyone turns the number into a contest, and exposes personal data.
